the-surgeon-s-daughter: Walter Scott's tale, part of his Chronicles of the Canongate, follows a young Scottish woman whose quiet life is upended by love and ambition. The story travels from a Fife village to the dangers of British India, where surgeons served the empire. Shorter than his great historical novels, it shows Scott's gift for character in a more intimate key.
the-king-of-the-dark-chamber: Tagore's symbolic play centers on a king whom no one has ever seen — his queen longs for his presence while priests and courtiers trade in empty ritual. Is he real, or only a dream of power? The Nobel laureate's haunting drama explores faith, love, and the human need for the unseen, in prose of great beauty.
the-blunderer: Molière's early farce follows Lélie, a well-meaning young lover whose every scheme to win his lady goes hilariously wrong. Servants scheme, masters bungle, and confusion piles upon confusion until all is resolved. Written when the playwright was still touring the provinces, L'Étourdi already sparkles with the comic genius that would conquer Paris.
princess-polly-s-gay-winter: Amy Brooks continues the adventures of her cheerful heroine Princess Polly through a lively winter season. Sleigh rides, parties, and small scrapes with friends fill a story written to delight young girls. Part of a long-running series, it offers the cozy, old-fashioned charm that made Polly a favorite.
quotations-from-the-pg-collected-works-o: This little volume gathers memorable lines from the novels and tales of Sir Gilbert Parker, the Canadian-born bestselling author. His stories of French Canada and the North were beloved on both sides of the Atlantic, and these quotations distill their spirit. A handy collection for lovers of Parker's romantic, adventurous fiction.
the-moccasin-maker: E. Pauline Johnson — the Mohawk poet and performer — gathers stories of Indigenous life in this moving collection. Her tales honor her mother's English heritage and her father's Mohawk blood with equal love. Written with grace and quiet power, the book preserves voices and traditions that were already fading when she wrote.
poems-of-power: Ella Wheeler Wilcox gathers verses meant to strengthen and inspire — poems of courage, will, and the power of positive thought. Her plain-spoken optimism made her the most popular inspirational poet of her age. Readers seeking encouragement in rhyme will find her at her most rousing here.
cap-n-dan-s-daughter: Joseph Lincoln — the beloved storyteller of Cape Cod — introduces Cap'n Dan's daughter in this warm tale of seafaring folk. Old salts, village gossip, and a young woman's romance fill pages rich in Down-East dialect and character. Lincoln's affection for his native coast made him one of America's most cherished regional writers.
the-wentworth-letter: In 1842, Joseph Smith wrote this famous letter to newspaper editor John Wentworth explaining the beliefs of the Latter-day Saints. Its clear statement of Mormon doctrine — including the Articles of Faith still recited today — became one of the church's foundational documents. Essential reading for understanding the LDS faith in its founder's own words.
the-tale-of-brownie-beaver: Arthur Scott Bailey's animal stories taught young children about nature through gentle adventure, and Brownie Beaver is a favorite. The busy beaver's dam-building and pond life unfold in simple, engaging prose. Part of Bailey's beloved Sleepy-Time Tales, perfect for bedtime reading.
philosophical-letters-of-friedrich-schil: The young Schiller pours his philosophical passion into these letters on God, freedom, and the meaning of life. Written before his great plays, they reveal the thinker behind the dramatist. For admirers of Schiller, an essential glimpse of his restless, searching mind.
the-works-of-frederick-schiller: This collected edition gathers the plays, poems, histories, and essays of Friedrich Schiller — Germany's beloved poet of freedom. From Wilhelm Tell to the Wallenstein trilogy, from the Ode to Joy to his histories of the Thirty Years War, his works shaped a nation's soul. An indispensable library for lovers of German literature.
the-doctor-s-daughter: Writing as Vera, the author tells the story of a doctor's daughter — her family, her suitors, and her choices in a close-knit community. Gentle romance and domestic drama unfold in the Victorian manner. A pleasant period novel for readers who enjoy old-fashioned storytelling.
the-whistling-mother: Grace Richmond — beloved author of the Red Pepper Burns stories — centers this novel on a cheerful, whistling mother whose optimism carries her family through hard times. Domestic trials, young love, and small-town life unfold with Richmond's warm humor. A cozy, big-hearted story from one of America's favorite storytellers.
in-the-quarter: Robert Chambers — later famous for The King in Yellow — sets this early novel among American art students in Paris's Latin Quarter. Studios, cafés, and young love fill a story drawn from his own student days. A romantic glimpse of bohemian Paris in the 1890s.
note-book-of-an-english-opium-eater: De Quincey adds to his famous Confessions with these notebooks — fragments of memory, dream, and reflection from the opium-eater's later years. His extraordinary prose turns personal odds and ends into literature. For admirers of one of English's most singular stylists.
miss-ludington-s-sister: Edward Bellamy — famous for the utopian Looking Backward — weaves a romantic tale touched by the supernatural around Miss Ludington and her mysterious sister. Love across the boundary of death gives the story its haunting charm. An unusual, tender novel from a surprising pen.
the-miser: Molière's classic comedy gives us Harpagon — the miser whose love of money poisons his family and his suitors' hopes. L'Avare remains one of the funniest plays ever written, its hero's obsession both hilarious and all too human. A masterpiece of comic character that never ages.
in-camp-on-the-big-sunflower: Lawrence Leslie's boys' camping story follows young campers on the Big Sunflower — their adventures, mishaps, and the lessons of outdoor life. Wholesome early-twentieth-century fun for young readers who loved the great outdoors. A cheerful period piece of American boyhood.
the-white-feather: Wodehouse's school novel centers on a boy accused of cowardice — the white feather — who must redeem himself in the boxing ring and win back his honor. A story of pluck and redemption from the master's school-days period. Early Wodehouse, already sparkling with wit.
a-biography-of-edmund-spenser: John Hales's study traces the life of Edmund Spenser — poet of The Faerie Queene — through Elizabethan Ireland and the English court. the-american-union-speaker: John Philbrick's speaker gathers patriotic orations and readings for school declamation — Webster, Everett, and the great voices of the Union. within-you-is-the-power: Henry Thomas Hamblin's New Thought classic teaches that within you is the power to shape your life — through right thinking and faith. rujub-the-juggler: Henty's Indian tale follows Rujub the juggler through the Mutiny's perils — a boy hero, a faithful native friend, and hairbreadth escapes. business-correspondence-vol-1-how-to-wri: This anonymous manual teaches the lost art of the business letter — form, tone, and clarity for every commercial occasion. the-yeoman-adventurer: George W. Gough's yeoman adventurer seeks his fortune in the new world — a tale of pluck and pioneer spirit. Honest adventure in the old style. A rousing story for boys. Clearings, canoes, and honest toil reward his stout English heart.
with-buller-in-natal-or-a-born-leader: Henty's boy hero serves with Buller in Natal during the Boer War — a born leader among soldiers. Spion Kop, Ladysmith, and the relief column fill these pages.
